2. Facts relevant for disposal of the instant civil appeal is that respondent no.1 herein as writ-petitioner filed the writ petition before the High Court respondent no. 6, giving decision of disposal of the appeal dated 11.09.2012 filed by the writ-petitioner against the decision of his force retirement passed by the writ-respondent no. 3, in Departmental Case No.13 of 2012 and also seeking direction upon the writ-respondents to reinstate the writ-petitioner in his previous post of Superintendent Engineer of Dhaka WASA impleading the impugned judgment and order passed by the appeal committee dated 07.04.2013 against the force retirement of the writ-petitioner by the writ-respondent no.3 in Departmental Case No.13 of 2012, contending inter alia, that the writ-petitioner was appointed as Assistant Engineer in the Dhaka WASA's R.P.E.M Circle on 02.08.1984 and from then he had been serving his duty with sincerity and full satisfaction of the authority concerned. After working in various posts and positions, he was promoted on 15.11.2009 to the post of Superintendent Engineer and was assigned with the charge of Plant Manager of Mineral Water brand `Shanti.' on 07.12.2009. While performing the duty as Superintendent Engineer, the respondent no.3 brought some allegations of misconduct, corruption and negligence against the writ-petitioner and thereby depart-mental case no.13 of 2012 was started and he was placed under suspension vide order dated 24.04.2012 under section 44(1) of “ঢাকা পানি সরবরাহ ও পয়:নিষ্কাশন কর্তৃপক্ষ (কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারী) চাকুরী প্রবিধানমালা, ২০১০” (hereinafter referred to as `Probidhanmala, 2010') and thereafter, attached to the office of respondent no.4. On 02.05.2012 the writ-petitioner made a representation requesting the respondent no.3 for withdrawing his suspension. Later, he filed an appeal on 04.06.2012 to the respondent not, for withdrawing the illegal suspension order. But without paying any heed to it the WASA authority illegally formed a 02(two) members inquiry committee to investigate into the allegations bought against the writ-petitioner. The writ-petitioner was not served with 1st show cause notice, rather on 23.07.2012 he received 2nd show cause notice whereby he was asked to show cause as to why he should not be dis-missed from service under Section 39(1)(kha) (ee) i.e ধারা-৩৯(১)(খ)(ঈ) of the Probidhanmala, 2010, to which he replied on 06.08.2012. Subsequently, considering his entire service record and other related matters, the writ-petitioner was awarded the punishment of force retirement on 30.08.2012 and accordingly the departmental case no.13 of 2012 was disposed of. Against the aforesaid order of force retirement, the writ-petitioner filed a departmental appeal to the Chairman, Dhaka WASA on 11.09,012. Thereafter, a 03(three) members Appeal Committee was constituted, who after hearing recommended to reinstate the writ-petitioner in his previous post with all arrear benefits. The said order was communicated to the writ-respondent no.3 for implementation, but to no avail. Thereafter, the respondent no.6 vide the impugned memo dated 25.07.2013 communicated that the appeal filed by the writ-petitioner was dismissed by the Board of Dhaka WASA. Upon receiving the impugned memo dated 25.07.2013 the writ-petitioner filed two review petitions to the writ-respondent no.2 on 21.08.2013 and 10.06.2014 respectively, which remain without any response. Hence, the writ-petition. 

 "I. Because the appeal was rejected as per provision of law, the appellate authority is not bound to implement the decision of the appeal committee and on the basis of the certain allegations of misconduct as well as inefficiency and thereupon, a regular Departmental Case being no.13 of 2012 has been started and as per provision of law after completion of departmental proceeding, the authority gave punishment to the writ-petitioner and as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside for the ends of justice. 

 9. Mr. A. M. Masum, learned Advocate, appearing for the appellant submits that the High Court Division erred in law in not holding that the departmental appeal preferred by the respondent no.1-writ-petitioner was rejected as per law and the appellate authority is not bound to implement the decision of the appeal committee and as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. He next submits that upon some specific allegations a regular departmental case being no.13 of 2012 was started against the respondent no.1 writ-petitioner and in compliance with all procedure, inquiry was held and pursuant to the provision of relevant law the authority concerned awarded punishment upon respondent no.1 writ-petitioner and as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. He lastly submits that due to the negligence and latches of the Advocate, the appellant did not appear before the Hugh Court Division during hearing of the Rule, as a result of which he could not agitate any submission which prejudiced him as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. 

 12. It appears from the record that respondent no.1 writ petitioner was a permanent employee of Dhaka WASA and the conditions of the service of a permanent employee of Dhaka WASA is regulated by the Probidhanmala, 2010. Again, if any departmental proceeding is initiated against any permanent employee of Dhaka WASA a major penalty can be imposed and in that case detailed procedure regarding formation and constitution of an inquiry is laid down in the Probidhanmala, 2010. 

 14. The quoted section mandates that where there is a scope to impose major punishment in a departmental proceeding in that case the inquiry committee must consist of either 01(one) member or 03(three) members who must not below in the grade/rank of the delinquent employee. 

 15. It appears from the materials on record that the respondent no.1-writ-petitioner was placed under suspension for some allegations of misconduct, corruption and negligence. Again, a depart-mental case no.13 of 2012 was started against him and the authority concerned vide order dated 19.06.2012, constituted an inquiry committee constituted of 02(two) members headed by one Uttam Kumar Roy, Commercial Manager of Dhaka WASA and the other member was one Kazi Wasiuddin, Executive Magistrate, who used to work in Dhaka WASA on deputation, at the relevant time. It is pertinent to mention here that pursuant to section 42(2)(Ga) of the Probidhanmala, 2010, there is no scope to constitute an inquiry committee consisting of 02(two) members. Moreover, on perusal of memo date 19.06.2012 signed by the Secretary, Dhaka WASA it appears that the other member of the constituted inquiry committee i.e. Kazi Wasiuddin being an Executive Magistrate was under in grade/rank than that of the respondent no.1 writ-petitioner, which is a gross violation of section 42(2)(Ga) of the Probidhanmala, 2010. 

 17. In the case of Ansar V.D.P Unnayan Bank Vs. Ajoy Kumar Ladh and others, reported in 30 ALR (AD) (2024)194, this Division held: 

 "From the above rule, it is crystal clear that to impose higher punishment the authority may appoint an inquiry officer to inquiry into the matter or to form a inquiry committee consisting of three members, but in the instant case it is admitted fact that the inquiry committee was formed by two persons and it is our considered view the whole inquiry proceeding suffers from lack of jurisdiction and the authority relying on such inquiry report committed serious error of law in awarding the punishment to the respondent no. 1." 

 18. Again, on perusal of charge form it appears that charge was framed against the respondent no.1 writ-petitioner in the departmental case no.13 of 2012 under section 38(Ka)(Kha) and (Gha) of the Probidhanmala, 2010. But on perusal of annexure-M it is evident that though the charge was framed under section 38(Ka)(Kha) and (Gha) of the Probidhanmala, 2010, but the respondent no.1 writ petitioner was placed in force retirement pursuant to section 10 (Kha) of the ঢাকা পানি সরবরাহ ও পয়:নিষ্কাশন কর্তৃপক্ষ কর্মচারী (অবসরভাতা ও অবসর জনিত সুবিধাদি) প্রবিধানমালা, ১৯৯৭. Moreover, force retirement has not been incorporated as a mode of major punishment in the section 39 of the Probidhanmala, 2010. 

 19, By now it is a settled principle of law that framing of charge in one law in a departmental case but later on punishment is awarded upon a different law in the same departmental case is not permissible and at the same time it is also violation of principles of Natural Justice. 

 22. It is pertinent to mention here that the appeal committee was constituted to make its recommendation so that on the basis of such recommendation the Board could adjudicate the appeal filed by the respondent no.1-writ-petitioner. Section 47(3) of the Probidhanmala, 2010, man-dates that the appeal committee can give any decision which in their opinion be considered as just and proper. But in the instant case, the Board of Dhaka WASA, ignoring the recommendation of the appeal committee most arbitrarily and illegally rejected the appeal filed by the respondent no.1 writ-petitioner. 

 23. Regarding ground no.2 of the leave granting order our considered view is that, the High Court Division considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as the relevant provisions of law and materials on record discussed the matter elaborately and thereby arrived at a decision as a result of this made the Rule absolute with direction. 

 24. It is a settled principle of law that if a suit or a writ petition, whatever it may be is disposed of considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as the relevant laws and materials on record, in that case there is no scope to interfere with that decision even if it can be passed by an ex-parte hearing. 

 26. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the discussions made above, we are of the view that the High Court Division after discussing all the aspects of this case arrived at a decision justifiably and rightly and as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division does not call for any interference by this Division.
